title: Pilot: Bhishma's Vow, and the Forest of Naimisha

ending.reason: The Rishi of Naimisha has finished asking for the Bharata, the history Vyasa composed and Vaisampayana recited at Janamejaya's snake sacrifice. The question is a complete speech turn, and it is the hook the rest of the telling answers. Sauti's reply begins at Book 1 §1 ¶6.

segments.label: Cold open: Bhishma's vow
segments.note: Book 1 §100 ¶10–11, Sambhava Parva. Vaisampayana is telling Janamejaya how Devavrata took the vow.

segments.label: Sauti arrives at Naimisha
segments.note: Book 1 §1 ¶1–5, Anukramanika Parva, read in order from the invocation.

lines.speaker: vaisampayana
lines.text: Vaisampayana continued,
lines.tts_text: Vaisampayana continued,

lines.speaker: vaisampayana
lines.text: O king, the son of Ganga, devoted to truth, having ascertained the scruples of the chief of the fishermen, then said, moved thereto by the desire of benefiting his father,
lines.tts_text: O king, the son of Ganga, devoted to truth, having ascertained the scruples of the chief of the fishermen, then said, moved thereto by the desire of benefiting his father,

lines.speaker: bhishma
lines.text: Chief of fishermen, thou best of men, listen to what I say in the presence of these assembled kings.
lines.tts_text: Chief of fishermen, thou best of men, listen to what I say in the presence of these assembled kings.

lines.speaker: bhishma
lines.text: Ye kings, I have already relinquished my right to the throne, I shall now settle the matter of my children.
lines.tts_text: Ye kings, I have already relinquished my right to the throne, I shall now settle the matter of my children.

lines.speaker: bhishma
lines.text: O fisherman, from this day I adopt the vow of Brahmacharya (study and meditation in celibacy).
lines.tts_text: O fisherman, from this day I adopt the vow of Brahmacharya.
lines.direction: a sacred vow before assembled kings

lines.speaker: bhishma
lines.text: If I die sonless, I shall yet attain to regions of perennial bliss in heaven!
lines.tts_text: If I die sonless, I shall yet attain to regions of perennial bliss in heaven!
lines.direction: a sacred vow before assembled kings

lines.speaker: vaisampayana
lines.text: Vaisampayana continued,
lines.tts_text: Vaisampayana continued,

lines.speaker: vaisampayana
lines.text: Upon these words of the son of Ganga, the hair on the fisherman's body stood on end from glee, and he replied,
lines.tts_text: Upon these words of the son of Ganga, the hair on the fisherman's body stood on end from glee, and he replied,

lines.speaker: dasa
lines.text: I bestow my daughter!
lines.tts_text: I bestow my daughter!

lines.speaker: vaisampayana
lines.text: Immediately after, the Apsaras and the gods with diverse tribes of Rishis began to rain down flowers from the firmament upon the head of Devavrata and exclaimed,
lines.tts_text: Immediately after, the Apsaras and the gods with diverse tribes of Rishis began to rain down flowers from the firmament upon the head of Devavrata and exclaimed,

lines.speaker: devas_chorus
lines.text: This one is Bhishma (the terrible).
lines.tts_text: This one is Bhishma.

lines.speaker: vaisampayana
lines.text: Bhishma then, to serve his father, addressed the illustrious damsel and said,
lines.tts_text: Bhishma then, to serve his father, addressed the illustrious damsel and said,

lines.speaker: bhishma
lines.text: O mother, ascend this chariot, and let us go unto our house.
lines.tts_text: O mother, ascend this chariot, and let us go unto our house.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: That vow made Devavrata into Bhishma.
lines.tts_text: That vow made Devavrata into Bhishma.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The story that leads there begins in the forest of Naimisha.
lines.tts_text: The story that leads there begins in the forest of Naimisha.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Om!
lines.tts_text: Om!

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Having bowed down to Narayana and Nara, the most exalted male being, and also to the goddess Saraswati, must the word Jaya be uttered.
lines.tts_text: Having bowed down to Naaraayana and Nahruh, the most exalted male being, and also to the goddess Saraswathi, must the word Jaya be uttered.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Ugrasrava, the son of Lomaharshana, surnamed Sauti, well-versed in the Puranas, bending with humility, one day approached the great sages of rigid vows, sitting at their ease, who had attended the twelve years' sacrifice of Saunaka, surnamed Kulapati, in the forest of Naimisha.
lines.tts_text: Ugrasrava, the son of Lomaharshana, surnamed Sauti, well-versed in the Puranas, bending with humility, one day approached the great sages of rigid vows, sitting at their ease, who had attended the twelve years' sacrifice of Shownuhkuh, surnamed Koolapati, in the forest of Naimisha.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Those ascetics, wishing to hear his wonderful narrations, presently began to address him who had thus arrived at that recluse abode of the inhabitants of the forest of Naimisha.
lines.tts_text: Those ascetics, wishing to hear his wonderful narrations, presently began to address him who had thus arrived at that recluse abode of the inhabitants of the forest of Naimisha.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Having been entertained with due respect by those holy men, he saluted those Munis (sages) with joined palms, even all of them, and inquired about the progress of their asceticism.
lines.tts_text: Having been entertained with due respect by those holy men, he saluted those Moonees with joined palms, even all of them, and inquired about the progress of their asceticism.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Then all the ascetics being again seated, the son of Lomaharshana humbly occupied the seat that was assigned to him.
lines.tts_text: Then all the ascetics being again seated, the son of Lomaharshana humbly occupied the seat that was assigned to him.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Seeing that he was comfortably seated, and recovered from fatigue, one of the Rishis beginning the conversation, asked him,
lines.tts_text: Seeing that he was comfortably seated, and recovered from fatigue, one of the Rishis beginning the conversation, asked him,

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: Whence comest thou, O lotus-eyed Sauti, and where hast thou spent the time?
lines.tts_text: Whence comest thou, O lotus-eyed Sauti, and where hast thou spent the time?

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: Tell me, who ask thee, in detail.
lines.tts_text: Tell me, who ask thee, in detail.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Accomplished in speech, Sauti, thus questioned, gave in the midst of that big assemblage of contemplative Munis a full and proper answer in words consonant with their mode of life.
lines.tts_text: Accomplished in speech, Sauti, thus questioned, gave in the midst of that big assemblage of contemplative Moonees a full and proper answer in words consonant with their mode of life.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Sauti said,
lines.tts_text: Sauti said,

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Having heard the diverse sacred and wonderful stories which were composed in his Mahabharata by Krishna-Dwaipayana, and which were recited in full by Vaisampayana at the Snake-sacrifice of the high-souled royal sage Janamejaya and in the presence also of that chief of Princes, the son of Parikshit, and having wandered about, visiting many sacred waters and holy shrines, I journeyed to the country venerated by the Dwijas (twice-born) and called Samantapanchaka where formerly was fought the battle between the children of Kuru and Pandu, and all the chiefs of the land ranged on either side.
lines.tts_text: Having heard the diverse sacred and wonderful stories which were composed in his Mahabharata by Krishna Dwaipayana, and which were recited in full by Vaisampayana at the Snake-sacrifice of the high-souled royal sage Janamejaya and in the presence also of that chief of Princes, the son of Puhrikshit, and having wandered about, visiting many sacred waters and holy shrines, I journeyed to the country venerated by the Dweejuhs and called Samantapanchaka where formerly was fought the battle between the children of Kuru and Pandu, and all the chiefs of the land ranged on either side.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Thence, anxious to see you, I am come into your presence.
lines.tts_text: Thence, anxious to see you, I am come into your presence.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Ye reverend sages, all of whom are to me as Brahma; ye greatly blessed who shine in this place of sacrifice with the splendour of the solar fire: ye who have concluded the silent meditations and have fed the holy fire; and yet who are sitting—without care, what, O ye Dwijas (twice-born), shall I repeat, shall I recount the sacred stories collected in the Puranas containing precepts of religious duty and of worldly profit, or the acts of illustrious saints and sovereigns of mankind?
lines.tts_text: Ye reverend sages, all of whom are to me as Brahma; ye greatly blessed who shine in this place of sacrifice with the splendour of the solar fire: ye who have concluded the silent meditations and have fed the holy fire; and yet who are sitting—without care, what, O ye Dweejuhs, shall I repeat, shall I recount the sacred stories collected in the Puranas containing precepts of religious duty and of worldly profit, or the acts of illustrious saints and sovereigns of mankind?

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The Rishi replied,
lines.tts_text: The Rishee replied,

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: The Purana, first promulgated by the great Rishi Dwaipayana, and which after having been heard both by the gods and the Brahmarshis was highly esteemed, being the most eminent narrative that exists, diversified both in diction and division, possessing subtile meanings logically combined, and gleaned from the Vedas, is a sacred work.
lines.tts_text: The Purana, first promulgated by the great Rishee Dwaipayana, and which after having been heard both by the gods and the Brahmarshis was highly esteemed, being the most eminent narrative that exists, diversified both in diction and division, possessing subtile meanings logically combined, and gleaned from the Vedas, is a sacred work.

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: Composed in elegant language, it includeth the subjects of other books.
lines.tts_text: Composed in elegant language, it includeth the subjects of other books.

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: It is elucidated by other Shastras, and comprehendeth the sense of the four Vedas.
lines.tts_text: It is elucidated by other Shastras, and comprehendeth the sense of the four Vedas.

lines.speaker: naimisha_rishis
lines.text: We are desirous of hearing that history also called Bharata, the holy composition of the wonderful Vyasa, which dispelleth the fear of evil, just as it was cheerfully recited by the Rishi Vaisampayana, under the direction of Dwaipayana himself, at the snake-sacrifice of Raja Janamejaya?
lines.tts_text: We are desirous of hearing that history also called Bharata, the holy composition of the wonderful Vyasa, which dispelleth the fear of evil, just as it was cheerfully recited by the Rishee Vaisampayana, under the direction of Dwaipayana himself, at the snake-sacrifice of Raja Janamejaya?
